versions.changelog: 0.0.3.0: Adds the plugin image. 0.0.2.0: Disabling the plugin returns sign-in to normal (users are handed back immediately and switched back to 2FA, with their sessions revoked, when it is enabled again); uninstall restores Jellyfin's default lockout, resets failed-login counters and deletes the SMTP password file. Failures through the proxy can no longer block LAN/Tailscale sign-in; the failure throttle is race-free and groups IPv6 by /64. Fixes in the recovery script (user names with quotes, exit codes), dropped code emails, health checks and configuration handling.

0.0.2.0: Disabling the plugin returns sign-in to normal (users are handed back immediately and switched back to 2FA, with their sessions revoked, when it is enabled again); uninstall restores Jellyfin's default lockout, resets failed-login counters and deletes the SMTP password file. Failures through the proxy can no longer block LAN/Tailscale sign-in; the failure throttle is race-free and groups IPv6 by /64. Fixes in the recovery script (user names with quotes, exit codes), dropped code emails, health checks and configuration handling.
0.0.1.0: initial version. Emailed one-time code for sign-ins through the reverse proxy; password-only sign-in for direct LAN/Tailscale connections.

name: Jelly2FA
description: Requires an emailed one-time code (typed directly after the password) for sign-ins that arrive through the reverse proxy. Direct LAN/Tailscale sign-ins use the password only. No client changes needed.
overview: Email-code two-factor authentication for remote sign-ins
